newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua's ex-president defends sugar mill sale.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua's ex-president defends sugar mill sale.

text.p: Nicaragua's ex-president Violeta Chamorro on Monday defended foreign investors who bought a sugar mill during her term of office and added she was prepared to explain and detail her actions if anyone thought she had acted illegally.
In an open letter published Monday, Chamorro criticised incumbent President Arnoldo Aleman for suing the owners of the Victoria de Julio mill, the country's largest sugar producing facility.
"If anyone believes that I actly badly they should ask me to account for my actions and not those who believed in me and in Nicaragua," Chamorro said.
AGROINSA, whose shareholders include ED&F Man and Swiss-based Nouveau Latin America, bought Victoria de Julio in a 1993 privatization during Chamorro's government.

Now, the Attorney General's Office has accused the shareholders of AGROINSA of buying the mill at a price below its true value and in "unclear" circumstances. A local jury is currently studying the Attorney General Office's request to annul the privatization.

Victoria de Julio has suffered a chequered ownership history. It was once the property of the Somoza dynasty that ruled this Central American nation until being overthrown in 1979 by the Sandinista revolution.

Under the Sandinistas, the mill was state run and re-equipped with machinery provided by Cuban and the former Soviet Union. Three years after Chamorro defeated the Sandinistas in 1990 elections, the mill was sold to AGROINSA.

Chamorro followers backed her criticism of Aleman's government. "The buyers followed the rules imposed by the state and now the state alleges that they be annuled because of errors that the same state supposedly committed. it is absurd," Tomas Delaney, an ex-Chamorro advisor said.
Delaney said annul the mill privatization would throw into doubt all other sell-offs from Chamorro's government and jeopardise future plans to privatise state utilities.
